messages:
Maya S: DispatchBot blocked publish for redwood/api:canary-2026-03-21-multiarch — failure: manifest list digest doesn't match signed manifest (cosign verification failed) :frown:
DispatchBot: publish blocked — manifestlist.digest (sha256:5f2a...) != signed.manifest.digest (sha256:7d9c...). Policy: require exact-match between signed manifest and registry manifestlist. See /runbooks/image-provenance
Liam R: This is odd — builder logs show cosign signed the image manifest for amd64 and arm64 separately, then `manifestify` assembled the manifestlist. Could the manifestlist reordering change the digest?
Maya S: Yes, we recently changed the manifestlist generator to sort by platform for determinism, but the cosign attest step signs per-arch manifests before manifestlist is composed. If manifestlist is signed later or expected to match pre-sorted ordering, digests diverge.
Olga T: Short term: we should avoid rebuilding. Option A: pin canary to the previously-promoted digest (sha256:21e4...) and delay rollout. Option B: re-create a manifestlist that matches the signed digest and retag. Which is safer?
Liam R: Retagging to match the signed manifestlist is safer if we can reproduce the exact manifestlist bytes. That requires the exact manifestify version + ordering and injecting any annotation cosign used. Risky if we guess. Pin to last-known-good digest is lower risk.
DispatchBot: advisory — emergency manual-pin allowed. Operator must add `release:manual-pin` and `incident:manifest-drift` in comment. Manual pins are audited.
Maya S: OK let's pin to last-known-good digest and open a reconciliation task. Tell Product and hold the canary window for 30 minutes.
ReleaseLead Bot: change window scheduled — canary promotion paused until 2026-03-21T18:10:00Z to allow manual pin and verification.
Liam R: I'll run the copy to pin the tag to the last-good digest. Commands I'll use:
```
# fetch manifest for digest
aws ecr batch-get-image --repository redwood/api --image-ids imageDigest=sha256:21e4... --query images[0].imageManifest --output text > manifest.json
# put-image with canary tag
aws ecr put-image --repository redwood/api --image-manifest file://manifest.json --image-tag canary-2026-03-21-pinned
```
Maya S: Add the comment in DispatchBot UI: "release:manual-pin incident:manifest-drift ci.buildid=20260321-998" — we need traceability for the postmortem
Olga T: I'll watch the repro verification. Also create an incident for tracking: include hypothesis about cosign timing + manifestify ordering, and action to ensure we either sign the final manifestlist or sign after manifestlist composition.
DispatchBot: manual pin performed by Liam R — verification pending
Liam R: Verification logs: cosign verify against the pinned manifest passes for the constituent arch manifests but manifestlist digest still differs because of annotation ordering. However DispatchBot's provenance check now passes for the pinned tag (we treat pinned copy as trusted fallback).
ReleaseLead Bot: publish allowed for tag canary-2026-03-21-pinned (manual-pin fallback) — make sure release notes mention the hold
Maya S: Release notes line: "Canary promotion held; manual pin to last-known-good digest applied due to manifestlist/cosign digest drift. Root cause under investigation."
Olga T: Follow-ups: (1) update CI to sign after manifestlist is composed, or sign the manifestlist bytes instead of per-arch only, (2) add a pre-push check comparing manifestlist digest vs cosign signature digest, (3) run an audit of the last 24h for any other manifestlist drift events.
Liam R: I'll open PRs: one to change the signing step, one to add the pre-push check. I'll also drop the put-image and verification logs into the incident. ETA for PRs: today EOD.
Maya S: Thanks team. If DispatchBot flags anything else, escalate to #eng-oncall. Closing thread once incident + PR links in the incident ticket.
